newsitem.title: FRANCE: Major surprised if anything like 12 pass EMU test.
newsitem.headline: Major surprised if anything like 12 pass EMU test.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Friday he would be surprised if anything like 12 European Union countries qualified for monetary union in 1999 on the basis of the strict terms in the EU's Maastricht treaty.
"I would be surprised if by January 1, 1999, anything like 12 nations qualify for EMU on anything like a strict interpretation of the criteria," Major said at a Franco-British summit here.
Major said some countries were more than 100 percent above the target on the debt criterion "with no credible likelihood of meeting the criteria on a strict basis".
The European Commission said on Wednesday 12 of the 15 EU countries would pass the Maastricht test of trimming their public deficits to three percent of gross domestic product.
One of the other targets in the Maastricht treaty is that countries should trim government debt towards 60 percent of GDP.
